text: Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Lowen Ridge, according to a company filing and a statement from Transport Ministry official Mara Venn. The depot, expected to open in late 2027, will occupy 18 hectares on the eastern industrial fringe of the city and create about 240 jobs, including mechanics, dispatch staff and cleaners. The filing said the site was selected for its rail access, nearby freight corridor and lower land costs. Lowen Ridge council approved preliminary zoning changes on Tuesday, and mayor Elias Thorn called the project “the largest transport investment here in a generation.” Kestrelline said ground surveys would begin next month, with construction to start after winter permits are issued.
